statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail edges back to 21% as the index grinds lower through the power hour with crude re-firming, while Stress stays high at 78% on a ten-year yield at 2007 highs.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Tail sits at 21%, low in the watch band: the index has drifted lower through the power hour but still holds roughly 59% of its intraday range above a session low set hours ago and never retested, so deep retracement remains intact and repeated extension after failed pullbacks is absent. WTI has firmed back to 93.07 dollars and VIX to 16.03, which reads as a mild re-amplification rather than observed one-way structure. One narrow danger window is flagged for 14:00-15:00Z on Sep 29, when JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence print together and the conditional forecast maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES.
headline: Nasdaq-100 grinds lower into the cash close as crude re-firms; Tail edges back into the low watch band with Stress still high
body: As of the 19:00Z clock-hour, the final hour before the 20:00Z US cash close, the Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,316.82, down 291.31 points or 0.95%, after a gap-down open at 30,426.63 from Friday's 30,608.13 close. The index has slipped from 30,334.47 an hour earlier but still sits about 59% of the way up the 30,081.06-30,480.40 intraday range from a session low that was set hours ago and has not been retested, so retracement remains deep and repeated extension after failed pullbacks has not been observed. NQ futures trade 30,582.50, down 0.99%, roughly 225 points above their 30,357.75 low inside a 30,357.75-30,920.75 range, which places them a little below the midpoint after easing from 30,641.50 an hour ago. The S&P 500 at 7,689.93, down 0.69% within a 7,666.60-7,724.15 range, confirms a broad but orderly drift rather than an index-specific break. Both amplifiers have partially re-firmed rather than decayed further: WTI is 93.07 dollars, up 0.72% on the day against flat an hour earlier, Brent is 105.71 dollars, up 1.33%, and VIX is 16.03, up from 15.85 but still below its 16.62 session high. The rate regime remains the unresolved stress source rather than a path-risk source, with the ten-year yield at 5.24% against a 5.18% prior close and inside a 5.20-5.27% day range, and the thirty-year reported near 5.57%, the highest since 2004. Catalysts behind the session are the rejection of Iran's conditional proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which lifted crude, and dispersed technology internals in which Nvidia trades higher on its record 150 billion dollar buyback authorisation while several other large semiconductors remain weak. Shared Finviz context collected at 14:34Z is both partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, and older than the 90-minute freshness threshold at this assessment time; its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are explicitly non-real-time and were used only as weak background confirmation of broad sector weakness with high semiconductor dispersion, never as live price-path evidence. Taken together this reads as an orderly, dispersion-driven drawdown that is still mean-reverting inside a high-yield regime, with a modest late-session re-amplification from crude and volatility, which places Tail at 21% with Stress at 78% and Confidence at 88%.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours ran from a calm late-Friday regime with Tail near 9-14% into an overnight repricing that lifted Tail into the 21-24% watch band from the 03:00Z hour onward, while Stress climbed from 72% to the mid-80s. Two hours printed in the elevated band: 09:00Z at 26% during the European morning as crude extended, and 14:00Z at 27% as the US cash session traded down toward its low. The last four hours eased to 23%, 20%, 20% and 19% as the index recovered off the low and crude gave up its gain. Confidence improved steadily from 77% to 88% as live price-path and cross-asset evidence accumulated. Historical entries are the values published at the time and are not restated with later information.
outlookSummary: The conditional forecast keeps the watch band across the 19:00Z power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, which remain the highest near-term slots because an unfilled gap-down day leaves little time to mean-revert if a late second leg develops. After the close the path eases into the low band through the evening and Asian hours, on the explicit assumption that no fresh US-Iran or Strait of Hormuz headline arrives, while Stress stays high on the near-106 dollar Brent and 5.24% ten-year backdrop. The watch band returns from 07:00Z as European cash hours trade the rate move, and the single elevated slot falls at 14:00Z on Sep 29, when JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence both print inside the first hour of US cash trade with the Dallas Fed Services Index following at 14:30Z. Forecast values are conditional risk, not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.

If instead the session low breaks into the settlement, the watch band would become the floor rather than the ceiling for the hours that follow.

Conditional checkpoint: whether 30,081.06 survives the closing auction
Post-close liquidity thins, widening quotes without implying trend

Stress stays high because the 5.24% ten-year and near-$106 Brent backdrop is unchanged overnight.

Stress held high by the unresolved rate regime, not by price path

forecast.analysis: Late US evening futures, historically the calmest stretch of the NQ day, with no scheduled US release inside the hour. The forecast assumes the low-band path continues. The named invalidation is a headline-driven gap out of the evening range, not a continuation of anything observed during the cash session.
drivers: No scheduled US macro release inside this hour
Thin evening futures volume; small prints are not structural evidence

forecast.analysis: Final hour before the daily futures maintenance break and the Asian handover. Tail is at its lowest forecast level of the period because no catalyst is scheduled and the prior session range is expected to contain trade. Stress remains high on the rate and energy regime rather than on any expected path.
drivers: Runs into the futures maintenance break and Asian session handover
Lowest scheduled-catalyst density of the whole forecast period
Stress here is regime-driven, not driven by an anticipated price path

forecast.analysis: Tokyo cash open and the first non-US read on Monday's rate move. The conditional path stays in the low band. A risk-off Asian open would raise Stress first under the contract, and would lift Tail only if NQ then extended without retracing, which this forecast does not assume.
drivers: Tokyo cash open; first non-US read on Monday's US rate move
Asian risk-off would raise Stress before Tail under the contract
Working assumption: NQ holds inside its Monday range overnight

forecast.analysis: Asian morning. Tail ticks up marginally because Hormuz-related energy headlines have repeatedly arrived during Asian hours in recent sessions. That is an observation about catalyst timing, not an observed price structure, and it is why the move is one point rather than a band change.
drivers: Asian hours have carried several recent Hormuz and crude headlines
Catalyst-timing density, not observed NQ structure
Brent above $105 leaves headroom for a further energy impulse

Escalation requires extension through the Monday low without retracement
No scheduled US data inside this hour

forecast.analysis: The equivalent clock-hour a day earlier is where Tail first moved into the watch band on overnight rate repricing. That is a historical reference rather than a prediction that it repeats, so the forecast keeps Tail just below the band while flagging the hour as a recurring transition point.
drivers: Same clock-hour that began Monday's overnight repricing
Treated as a transition checkpoint, not as a repeating pattern
Stress steady on an unchanged rate and energy regime

forecast.analysis: Late Asian trade into the European pre-open. Tail holds just under the watch band. The forecast assumes dispersion between megacaps and semiconductors persists rather than resolving into a single direction, which is the main structural reason this reads as an orderly drawdown rather than a one-way path.
drivers: Late Asia into the European pre-open handover
Assumes megacap and semiconductor dispersion persists
Dispersion is the main structural reason Tail stays below the band

forecast.analysis: European pre-open hour. Stress edges to 75% as European rate futures begin to price Monday's US long-end move. Tail is unchanged, because repricing a rate level is a valuation event; it becomes a path event only if NQ subsequently trends without retracing.
drivers: European rate futures begin pricing Monday's US long-end move
Rate repricing raises Stress before it can raise Tail
Thirty-year at 5.57%, reported as the highest since 2004, is the anchor

forecast.analysis: Last low-band hour of the forecast, immediately before European cash trade. Tail at 19% reflects the approach of the European open rather than any observed structure. A quiet open would hold this level; a gap-down open would move the following hours up a band.
drivers: Final hour before European cash equities open
Tail at the top of the low band purely on session timing
Branch point: a gap-down European open lifts the following hours

forecast.analysis: European cash open. Tail enters the watch band because the European session is the first venue to trade Monday's US rate move in size, and the same hour on Monday opened a sustained watch-band stretch. This is treated as a conditional checkpoint, not as an observed repeat.

forecast.analysis: First hour after the 14:00Z releases. Tail steps back to the top of the watch band on the base case that price discovery is orderly and retracements occur. The contract allows a faster decline than this if the path mean-reverts cleanly, and a higher level only if extension continues without pullbacks.
